sources.locator: Complete 634-page PDF. §2.1 Definition 2.2, printed p. 42; §4.3 Definition 4.21 and Theorems 4.19–4.22, printed pp. 85–88; complete Theorem 4.25 proof, printed pp. 89–90.
sources.source_kind_detail: Full textbook PDF. Read the best-term definition and complete relevant robust-NSP/recovery arguments; Definition 4.21 at q=2 matches the IP-34 tail-l1 convention.

contents.name: §2.1 Definition 2.2: best s-term l1 approximation
contents.detail: The book minimizes over s-sparse vectors and notes largest-coordinate attainment. The local definition uses a finite coordinate-tail minimum; the companion lemma proves exact equivalence and attainment.

contents.name: §4.3 Definition 4.21: q-robust nullspace property
contents.detail: At q=2 the formula is exactly head l2 bounded by rho divided by sqrt(s) times tail l1 plus tau times the measurement residual.

contents.name: §4.3 Theorems 4.19–4.20: stable l1 recovery and cone inequality
contents.detail: These results support the recovery route; the local theorem proves its own cone estimate and constants.

contents.name: §4.3 Theorems 4.22 and 4.25: stable noisy recovery and complete proof
contents.detail: The complete Theorem 4.25 proof was read. The local proof derives the displayed constants rather than copying the book's stronger estimate.

contents.name: §4.3 quadratically constrained basis pursuit formulation
contents.detail: The source formulation motivates the feasible residual-ball problem; local proof establishes finite-dimensional attainment and the worked values.

sources.title: Shahar Mendelson, Holger Rauhut, and Rachel Ward, Improved Bounds for Sparse Recovery from Subsampled Random Convolutions
sources.locator: Complete 39-page paper. §2.1 Definition 2.1 and Theorem 2.2, printed pp. 4–5.
sources.source_kind_detail: Full author-hosted research paper. Read the exact robust-NSP formula and recovery theorem statement; the paper calls the result standard and does not prove it.

contents.name: §2.1 Definition 2.1: lq-robust nullspace property
contents.detail: For q=2 this is the exact tail-l1/head-l2 inequality with all vectors and all supports of size at most s.

contents.name: §2.1 Theorem 2.2: best-term and noise recovery bounds
contents.detail: The paper states the stable recovery rates and constants but does not supply a proof; the local theorem proves the claims and the example substitutes exact data.

contents.name: §2.1 best s-term error notation
contents.detail: The source uses the sparse-vector distance formulation; the local finite-coordinate argument proves its equality with the authored tail minimum.

sources.title: Antonin Chambolle and Thomas Pock, A First-Order Primal-Dual Algorithm for Convex Problems with Applications to Imaging
sources.locator: Complete 51-page report. §2, Algorithm 1, and §3.1, printed pp. 2–7.
sources.source_kind_detail: Full author-hosted research report. Read the saddle formulation, exact primal-dual recurrence, strict step condition, and stated convergence scope.

contents.name: §2 Algorithm 1: primal-dual hybrid-gradient recurrence and step condition
contents.detail: The authored procedure uses the exact recurrence and strict step-size condition. Its finite solver/checker wrapper and certificates are local additions; no finite discovery guarantee is imported.

contents.name: §3.1 proper closed convex primal-dual input framework
contents.detail: The report supplies the generic convexity precondition. The local lemma verifies that the specific l1 objective and residual-ball indicator meet it.
